title: Age-related hearing loss is gradual
text: Age-related hearing loss (presbycusis) usually comes on slowly over years, starting with high-pitched sounds and difficulty in noise, so the person adapts and often does not notice it. A regular check against earlier answers helps catch the change earlier.
source: World Health Organization. World report on hearing

title: Why finding it early matters
text: Untreated hearing loss is linked with social isolation, low mood and faster cognitive decline. Identifying it earlier and fitting hearing aids when needed supports communication and wellbeing; delay makes adjustment to aids harder.
source: Lancet Commission on hearing loss / WHO World report on hearing

title: Trouble in noise is an early sign
text: Difficulty following speech in a noisy place — a wedding, a market, a restaurant — while managing in a quiet room is one of the earliest everyday signs of hearing loss, because background noise masks the softer high-frequency sounds of speech first.
source: British Society of Audiology; WHO World report on hearing

title: hearWHO and proper testing
text: A questionnaire like this one is a prompt, not a diagnosis. WHO's free hearWHO app gives a quick digits-in-noise screen, and an RCI-registered audiologist can carry out full pure-tone audiometry to confirm the degree and type of any loss.

title: Sudden hearing loss is an emergency
text: A sudden drop in hearing, usually in one ear, over hours to a few days is a medical emergency (sudden sensorineural hearing loss). Prompt treatment within days gives the best chance of recovery — see a doctor or ENT the same day; do not wait for a monthly check.
source: Chandrasekhar SS, et al. Clinical practice guideline: sudden hearing loss (update). Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 161(1 Suppl):S1–S45
